part.name: Countertop beverage-machine assembly
part.description: Multi-solid appliance assembly with a rounded main housing, front closure panel and feet, rear service cover with ventilation ribs and handle trim, internal perforated support panel, selector controls, brewing interface, articulated steam wand, two cup-like accessories, and a vertical operating lever. The STEP model contains 56 solids and 532 faces; surface matching is based on face bounding boxes, orientation, area, and agreement with the supplied views.
part.symmetry_note: The primary housing, front panel, rear cover, feet, grille, and internal support panel are approximately symmetric about the vertical longitudinal center plane. The steam wand and some control/interface details are intentionally asymmetric. Two cup-like accessory solids form a visually paired but differently oriented set.

Section.name: Front closure and feet
features included: four corner support feet or bumpers
Section.function intent: Closes and protects the front side of the assembly, establishes the appliance footprint, and provides stable contact points with a supporting surface.
Section.physical behavior: The broad panel resists distributed contact and enclosure loads, while the surrounding shell transfers those loads into the main chassis. The four compliant-looking corner feet provide separated reaction points, reduce sliding, and accommodate small surface irregularities.
Section.geometry: A broad rounded rectangular plate backed by a deeper blended shell. Long planar regions are joined by cylindrical corner bands and freeform edge transitions. Four small rounded rectangular feet project from the outer face near the corners.
Section.location: At the negative-y end of the STEP assembly; seen as the large black rounded panel in the front view.

Section.name: Main U-frame housing
features included: left and right structural side walls
Section.function intent: Forms the primary load-bearing chassis, encloses internal components, and defines the open working bay beneath the brewing interface.
Section.physical behavior: The two side walls and bottom spine behave as a deep U-shaped frame. Their broad shell surfaces carry bending and torsional loads, while the rounded opening corners distribute stress and avoid sharp local concentrations.
Section.geometry: A large freeform shell-like solid extending through most of the appliance depth. It has broad side facets, a bottom web, curved upper and lower transitions, and a large rectangular/U-shaped clearance opening.
Section.location: Central body between the front closure and rear service cover.

Section.function intent: Closes the rear of the appliance while providing a removable or separately manufactured service enclosure.
Section.physical behavior: The shallow dished panel gains stiffness from its rolled perimeter and side returns. It resists distributed pressure and handling loads and transfers them to the main frame around its boundary.
Section.geometry: A shallow rounded rectangular cover with broad front and rear freeform fields, narrow side returns, a rolled upper edge, and smoothly blended corners.

Section.name: Rear ventilation grille

Section.physical behavior: The parallel ribs act as slender beams between their end regions. Their spacing permits airflow, while the repeated cylindrical profiles improve bending stiffness and remove sharp exposed edges.
Section.geometry: A regular array of long, small-radius horizontal cylinders positioned in front of the rear cover. Each rib has a cylindrical major surface and two planar end caps.

Section.physical behavior: The horizontal and vertical rods carry hand loads primarily in bending and transfer them through curved end transitions into the rear cover. Rounded sections reduce contact pressure and avoid sharp edges.
Section.geometry: A disconnected but coordinated tubular arrangement consisting of one upper horizontal cylinder, two long vertical cylinders, and several short freeform elbow pieces.

Section.function intent: Provides an internal protective screen or ventilated mounting wall while preserving airflow and reducing mass.
Section.physical behavior: The thin panel carries in-plane loads efficiently. The dense holes permit airflow but locally interrupt the stress field; the remaining ligaments distribute load across the array. The continuous perimeter maintains overall panel stiffness.
Section.geometry: A thin rounded rectangular plate with 109 inner wires reported on its perforated planar face. The hole walls are short cylinders normal to the panel, with planar circular termination faces.

part.name: Countertop beverage-machine assembly
part.description: Multi-solid appliance assembly with a rounded main housing, front closure panel and feet, rear service cover with ventilation ribs and handle trim, internal perforated support panel, selector controls, brewing interface, articulated steam wand, two cup-like accessories, and a vertical operating lever. The STEP model contains 56 solids and 532 faces; surface matching is based on face bounding boxes, orientation, area, and agreement with the supplied views.
part.symmetry_note: The primary housing, front panel, rear cover, feet, grille, and internal support panel are approximately symmetric about the vertical longitudinal center plane. The steam wand and some control/interface details are intentionally asymmetric. Two cup-like accessory solids form a visually paired but differently oriented set.

Section.name: Front closure and feet
features included: four corner support feet or bumpers
Section.function intent: Closes and protects the front side of the assembly, establishes the appliance footprint, and provides stable contact points with a supporting surface.
Section.physical behavior: The broad panel resists distributed contact and enclosure loads, while the surrounding shell transfers those loads into the main chassis. The four compliant-looking corner feet provide separated reaction points, reduce sliding, and accommodate small surface irregularities.
Section.geometry: A broad rounded rectangular plate backed by a deeper blended shell. Long planar regions are joined by cylindrical corner bands and freeform edge transitions. Four small rounded rectangular feet project from the outer face near the corners.
Section.location: At the negative-y end of the STEP assembly; seen as the large black rounded panel in the front view.

Section.name: Main U-frame housing

Section.function intent: Forms the primary load-bearing chassis, encloses internal components, and defines the open working bay beneath the brewing interface.
Section.physical behavior: The two side walls and bottom spine behave as a deep U-shaped frame. Their broad shell surfaces carry bending and torsional loads, while the rounded opening corners distribute stress and avoid sharp local concentrations.
Section.geometry: A large freeform shell-like solid extending through most of the appliance depth. It has broad side facets, a bottom web, curved upper and lower transitions, and a large rectangular/U-shaped clearance opening.
Section.location: Central body between the front closure and rear service cover.

Section.physical behavior: The shallow dished panel gains stiffness from its rolled perimeter and side returns. It resists distributed pressure and handling loads and transfers them to the main frame around its boundary.
Section.geometry: A shallow rounded rectangular cover with broad front and rear freeform fields, narrow side returns, a rolled upper edge, and smoothly blended corners.

Section.name: Rear ventilation grille
Section.function intent: Protects a rear opening while maintaining distributed airflow and preventing large-object ingress.
Section.physical behavior: The parallel ribs act as slender beams between their end regions. Their spacing permits airflow, while the repeated cylindrical profiles improve bending stiffness and remove sharp exposed edges.
Section.geometry: A regular array of long, small-radius horizontal cylinders positioned in front of the rear cover. Each rib has a cylindrical major surface and two planar end caps.

Section.physical behavior: The horizontal and vertical rods carry hand loads primarily in bending and transfer them through curved end transitions into the rear cover. Rounded sections reduce contact pressure and avoid sharp edges.
Section.geometry: A disconnected but coordinated tubular arrangement consisting of one upper horizontal cylinder, two long vertical cylinders, and several short freeform elbow pieces.

Section.name: Internal perforated support panel
Section.function intent: Provides an internal protective screen or ventilated mounting wall while preserving airflow and reducing mass.
Section.physical behavior: The thin panel carries in-plane loads efficiently. The dense holes permit airflow but locally interrupt the stress field; the remaining ligaments distribute load across the array. The continuous perimeter maintains overall panel stiffness.
Section.geometry: A thin rounded rectangular plate with 109 inner wires reported on its perforated planar face. The hole walls are short cylinders normal to the panel, with planar circular termination faces.
Section.location: Inside the main housing near the front side of the working cavity.

Section.name: Selector and indicator controls
Section.function intent: Provides the user interface for selecting an operating mode and visually indicating available or selected states.
Section.physical behavior: The dial transmits hand torque about its central axis. Its broad curved side provides grip, while the pointer and surrounding marks communicate angular position. The slots and dots function as visual indicators or vents with negligible primary structural load.
Section.geometry: A central rounded rotary body with a shallow top face and tapered sides, a narrow pointer insert, a curved thin indicator arc, several small raised pads, and three elongated rounded slots.

Section.name: Brewing-head and outlet interface
Section.function intent: Locates and supports the brewing or dispensing interface, receives an attached mating component, and transfers operating forces into the chassis.
Section.physical behavior: The circular housings distribute clamping and fluid-interface loads around their circumferences. Axial reaction is carried through the flange into the main housing, while the smaller outlet body guides the dispensed fluid and provides local attachment geometry.
Section.geometry: Several coaxial or nearly coaxial rounded housings with square-rounded and circular freeform profiles. The assembly includes broad annular faces, tapered side patches, a mounting flange, and a smaller central outlet body.
Section.location: Upper central portion of the open working bay.

Section.name: Steam-wand assembly
Section.function intent: Provides a movable fluid or steam outlet that can be positioned relative to a vessel.
Section.physical behavior: The joint permits angular repositioning while constraining translation. The tube carries internal pressure and bending from user handling, while the larger sleeve improves grip and thermally separates the hand from the smaller tube.
Section.geometry: An asymmetric chain of toroidal, cylindrical, planar, and freeform surfaces. A small swivel joint connects to a long tube, a larger cylindrical sleeve, and a curved terminal segment.

Section.physical behavior: Each vessel behaves as a thin-walled shell supported at its base. The flared walls provide internal volume and handling clearance. These solids are removable accessories rather than primary load-bearing appliance structure.
Section.geometry: Two separate rounded, tapered, approximately cup-shaped freeform solids. One is aligned with the assembly axes; the other is rotated, producing oblique face orientations in the STEP report.

Section.name: Vertical operating lever
Section.function intent: Provides a long manual moment arm for actuating or clamping the brewing mechanism.
Section.physical behavior: Hand force applied at the remote end creates torque about the lower pivot. The long cylindrical shaft carries bending, the smaller stem transfers shear and torque into the mechanism, and the conical transition reduces the stress concentration between diameters.
Section.geometry: A coaxial stepped lever composed of a small lower cylinder, a short conical shoulder, a long larger-diameter cylinder, and a planar circular end cap.
